en.title: iOS & Android Developer
en.keywords: Swift · SwiftUI · UIKit · Swift Concurrency · XCTest · CI/CD · Kotlin · Jetpack Compose
en.availability: Open to iOS and mobile roles in Skåne, Copenhagen or remote
en.profile: I am an iOS developer with a focus on UI/UX, something my mentor at Axis Communications singled out. For nearly five months in the iOS team there, I built live video controls and fixed bugs in a production app. I am now finishing my own app, Subtl, for the App Store. It creates captions with AI that runs right on the phone, and I am the only developer.

bullets: Built live video controls for microphone, speaker and PTZ (pan-tilt-zoom) in an iOS app that connects to cloud services and IoT devices, so users can listen, talk and control the camera from their phone.
Migrated selected asynchronous flows to async/await with strict concurrency checking, and created an interactive interface with SwiftUI Canvas.
Added Datadog and OpenTelemetry tracing to a multi-step flow, so the team can see where errors occur.
Delivered bug fixes, new components and Datadog analytics through pull requests that were reviewed and merged, in an agile team of iOS and Android developers.
experience.tech: Swift, SwiftUI, UIKit, async/await, Datadog, OpenTelemetry, Git, Jira
experience.note: My manager at Axis wrote in his letter: “We give him our best recommendation.” More recommendations on LinkedIn.

bullets: Built an Android chat app in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose on top of Weavy’s REST API, with MVVM (ViewModel and StateFlow), Hilt, Retrofit and token-based authentication with the token in DataStore.
experience.tech: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Coroutines, Hilt, Retrofit, DataStore, Git

projects.name: Subtl
projects.status: Independent app, preparing for App Store release
bullets: The app creates captions with AI speech recognition in English and Swedish and translates them locally, with no account, no uploads and no data collection.
Transcription runs in an actor under Swift 6, export burns captions into the video or writes SRT and WebVTT, and the five caption styles look the same in preview and export.
Built Ask Subtl on Apple’s Foundation Models. The assistant searches clips and transcripts through tool calling and proposes changes that the user must confirm.
Connected the app to Siri, Shortcuts and Spotlight via App Intents, added a Live Activity for background exports and built layouts for the foldable iPhone Duo. The app is in English and Swedish.
Wrote automated unit and UI tests for the flow from import to export, including dark mode and large text, and set up CI in GitHub Actions with static analysis and a release build.
projects.tech: Swift 6, SwiftUI, SpeechAnalyzer, Foundation Models, App Intents

projects.name: DeviceMonitor
projects.status: Grit Academy final project (Distinction), developed into my own app
bullets: A network monitor for iPhone and iPad that finds the devices on the local Wi-Fi network with TCP, ICMP and UDP probes and Bonjour, and charts latency, jitter and outages over time.
The monitoring engine runs in an actor and writes to SwiftData every 500 ms, with a versioned schema migration. Views only read immutable snapshots, never the database.

Apple Intelligence (Foundation Models) explains each device on the network without sending data to the cloud. Names and services from the network go in as fenced data to guard against prompt injection.
projects.tech: SwiftUI, SwiftData, Foundation Models, Swift Charts, Metal

projects.name: MetalVisualKit
bullets: Swift package that unprojects LiDAR depth data into about 49,000 3D points on the GPU and animates 1,400 particles in a compute shader. It has unit tests in XCTest, a demo app, CI and DocC.
projects.tech: Metal, ARKit, Swift Package Manager, XCTest, DocC

Lade till spårning med Datadog och OpenTelemetry i ett flöde med flera steg, så att teamet kan se i vilket av stegen felen uppstår.
Levererade buggrättningar, nya komponenter och Datadog-analys via pull requests som granskades och slogs ihop, i ett agilt team med iOS- och Androidutvecklare.
